Testing means checking what happens, not just noticing that a page opens. Test the happy path and the mistakes that real people make.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

A repeatable request checklist

  • Start the in-memory API fresh. GET the empty list. POST a valid student and record the returned ID and Location header.
  • GET that ID and check name/age. PUT a different name; GET again to prove persistence within this process. DELETE it; GET must return 404.
  • POST an invalid age, empty name, whitespace-only name and name longer than 80 characters; all should return 400. Send broken JSON and confirm rejection.
  • For EF examples restart without deleting the database and check that kept rows survive. For the secure API test 401, cross-owner access, stale versions and page-size limits.
  • A unit test isolates a service or validation rule. An integration test starts a test host with WebApplicationFactory<Program> and a separate test database. Never run destructive tests against a real student database.

OpenAPI and Swagger are related, not identical

Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi can generate an OpenAPI document. AddOpenApi registers generation; MapOpenApi exposes /openapi/v1.json in Development. A Swagger UI is a separate viewer. Install a compatible Swagger UI package and configure its endpoint to that JSON if you want an interactive web page. A .NET 10 template does not promise /swagger will exist by default. The supplied .http files work without Swagger.

Debug failures systematically

  • 404: check exact route, HTTP method and launch port. 400: inspect validation response and JSON Content-Type. 415: wrong request media type.
  • 500: inspect the server log and breakpoint locally. Do not return passwords, stack traces or connection strings to clients.
  • CS0246: missing using, file, namespace or NuGet restore. Unable to resolve service: add the missing DI registration.
  • No database table: run migrations. Cannot connect: check database service and connection string. 401: send a valid unexpired token. 409: fetch the latest version before editing.

Try it yourself

Design one positive and one negative test for PUT.

Worked answer

Positive: update an existing row then GET it. Negative: an invalid age must be rejected and must not change the stored row.

Why is “the response was 200” not enough?

Worked answer

The body might contain the wrong data. Check status, headers, response shape and stored state.

Run the repeatable HTTP checks

The downloadable project below is a console test runner. Start API project02 on port5100 in one terminal. Open this test project in another terminal and run dotnet run. Expected: eight PASS lines and All CRUD checks passed. Each check asserts status or stored values; a failed check throws.
